Cobb County by the numbers

What does the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court record?

Filed here: every Cobb County deed, plat, condominium floor plan, lien, UCC filing, general execution docket entry, military discharge, trade name and partnership. The Real Estate Division is the desk where your deed to a buyer lands, and where the cancellation of your old security deed appears once the loan is paid off.

Find it in Building C at 10 East Park Square in Marietta, beside the State Court Building. Recording is handled upstairs on the second floor and copies in the deed room on the first. Mail goes to P.O. Box 3430, Marietta, GA 30061. Weekday hours start at 8:30 and run until 5:00 in the afternoon, yet the recording and copy counters shut half an hour earlier. The number to call is 770-528-2000.

Because pickup times between the Postal Service and the county mail room have shifted, the clerk asks anyone racing a deadline to mail early and to skip late-afternoon e-filing on the final day.

Who is allowed to file a deed on paper in Cobb County?

Since January 1, 2025, Georgia law under House Bill 1292 requires people filing for themselves to e-file real estate documents. Every person who e-files must first pass identity verification, including a photo check, through the Clerks' Authority portal at efile.gsccca.org. That portal is the only one through which real estate documents can be e-filed.

Paper filing is still open to these groups:

  • Georgia-licensed attorneys
  • Mortgage lenders, whether Georgia licensed or exempt
  • Mortgage servicers
  • Georgia-licensed surveyors
  • Georgia-licensed title insurance companies
  • Georgia-licensed real estate brokers or salespersons
  • Any public official

A member of one of those groups who chooses to e-file has to be verified like anyone else. A seller working through a closing attorney or title company rarely touches the filing, because the closing office submits the deed. An owner who prepares and files a deed without an attorney is the person most affected, and should finish the identity check before the recording date.

How much does the Cobb County clerk charge to record a deed?

A deed costs $25.00 for its first page and nothing for pages after that, according to the schedule the clerk posted for January 1, 2020. Security deeds, assignments, satisfactions and cancellations fall under the same line. An online fee calculator on the clerk's site gives the exact total for a given filing. The counter takes cash, money orders, cashier's checks, certified checks and cards, though a cardholder paying in person must show ID and sign the charge slip.

Selected real estate filing fees posted by the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court
DocumentFirst pageAdded pages
Deeds, security deeds, assignments, satisfactions, cancellations$25.00$0.00
Plats$10.00$10.00
Liens, lis pendens, notices of commencement, fi. fas.$25.00$0.00
State and local tax liens and releases$5.00$2.00
Bonds and landlord bonds$25.00$0.00
Miscellaneous documents$5.00$2.00

Added cancellations, releases, satisfactions and assignments are priced per document in the clerk's schedule. One check can cover the recording fee and the tax, except for trade names. Write it to the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court.

What is the Georgia transfer tax and how is it paid in Cobb County?

Warranty deeds and quit claim deeds both arrive with a PT-61 and the transfer tax, paid when the deed is recorded, unless an exemption applies. The clerk points to O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 and 48-6-2. You fill the PT-61 out online and print it to submit with the deed. Lobby computers let you do that on site.

On its transfer tax page the Department of Revenue states the rate as $1 on the first $1,000 of the sale price, then 10 cents for every further $100, with any fraction counted as a full unit. Liability sits with the seller, though many contracts hand it to the buyer. Your settlement statement shows who paid.

Lenders face a second charge, the intangible recording tax on a long-term note secured by real estate, which the revenue department's fact sheet lists at $1.50 per $500 of the note. The clerk adds that a security deed has to be filed within 90 days of signing to avoid penalty and interest when the note runs past three years or is not exempt. Your buyer's lender cares about that rule far more than you do.

What does a Cobb County deed have to include?

For both warranty deeds and quit claim deeds the clerk lists identical requirements: the full legal description, the name of the party transferring, the name of the party receiving, and the grantor's signature with a witness and a notary. Nobody at the clerk's counter notarizes, so arrive with the deed already done by a commissioned Georgia notary.

The two deed types protect a buyer differently. A warranty deed is the usual choice in a purchase and carries a guarantee that title is good and marketable, which is why buyers and lenders ask for it. A quit claim deed passes only whatever interest the signer holds, with no promise that title is clear or free of liens. It tends to show up in transfers between relatives or into a family entity.

  • Use the full legal description from your last deed, not the street address.
  • Have the notary and the witness sign in the same sitting as the grantor.
  • Complete the PT-61 before you arrive.
  • Bring one payment that covers recording fee and tax.

How do I get copies and check that my old mortgage was cancelled?

Three ways exist to get a recorded document: print it from the clerk's website, copy it in the first-floor deed room, or mail in the request form with a self-addressed stamped envelope. Condo floor plans follow the same routes. After a payoff, the cancellation of a security deed normally goes back to the borrower unless the lender directs it elsewhere, which usually means the mortgage company. You can search the clerk's site to confirm it was filed. Lien payments never go through this office. They go to the lien holder.

Permits for fences, additions and similar work come from another office. The clerk's FAQ sends owners to Cobb County or to the City of Marietta, whichever covers the address.

The clerk's real estate page also links to the Filing Activity Notification System at fans.gsccca.org.

What should a Cobb County seller know about the county itself?

Cobb sits northwest of Atlanta and was carved out of former Cherokee land in 1832. Marietta is the seat and Mableton the largest city. The county spans about 345 square miles, and its 2020 population of 766,149 ranked third in the state. Kennesaw Mountain, the county's high point, rises between Kennesaw and Marietta.

The school district employs more than 15,000 people, the most of any employer, and the county hosts the Home Depot support center, the Weather Channel and the Lockheed Martin plant next to Dobbins Air Reserve Base. Interstates 75, 20, 285 and 575 run through it. The tax commissioner's office bills the county and school district, and the cities of Acworth, Austell, Kennesaw, Mableton, Marietta, Smyrna and Powder Springs bill their own taxes.

Street addresses in the county all count from the southwest corner of the Marietta town square. Liens that must be released before a deed can be recorded are a job for a closing attorney, since the clerk's staff cannot advise you.

More questions about Cobb County, GA Clerk of Superior Court

Which Cobb County office takes a deed for recording?

The Real Estate Division of the Cobb County Clerk of Superior Court, in Building C at 10 East Park Square in Marietta. Doors open weekdays at 8:30, the recording counters stop at 4:30 and the office closes at 5:00. Questions go to 770-528-2000.

Can I file my own deed on paper in Cobb County?

Usually not. Since January 1, 2025, people filing for themselves must e-file through efile.gsccca.org after verifying their identity with a photo check. Attorneys, lenders, servicers, surveyors, title companies, brokers and public officials may still file on paper.

What does recording a deed cost at the Cobb County clerk?

Twenty-five dollars for the first page and nothing for added pages, per the clerk's posted schedule. Transfer tax comes on top and is paid with the PT-61. The online fee calculator gives an exact total, and a single check can cover both.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Cobb County sale?

The law puts it on the seller, and the sales contract may move it to the buyer. The Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 on the first $1,000 of the price plus 10 cents per further $100. Check the settlement statement.

Does the Cobb County clerk notarize or give legal advice?

No on both counts. The clerk's office does not notarize, so bring a deed that is already signed before a notary with a witness. State law also bars the clerk's staff from giving legal advice, so a closing attorney should answer questions about what your deed should say.

Dekalb County by the numbers

What does the DeKalb County clerk's office do at a home sale?

Recording the deed that carries title from seller to buyer falls to the clerk's Real Estate Division, along with mortgages, plats, liens and other papers that touch land in DeKalb County. The office says it receives more than 204,500 real estate documents a year, and its records run back to 1842 because earlier books burned in a fire.

The clerk's FAQ describes three roles: clerk of court, registrar of land records, and collector of intangible and transfer taxes. In practice one office handles the recording, the transfer tax certification and the public index that a title examiner searches before closing.

The Census Bureau counts 267.74 land square miles in DeKalb and estimated 774,394 residents for 2025. The county seat is Decatur.

Where is the Real Estate Division and when is it open?

The division is on the ground floor at 556 N. McDonough Street, Decatur, GA 30030. The real estate page lists 404-687-3812 and weekday hours from half past eight in the morning until five in the afternoon The clerk's general information line is 404-371-2836.

Property records are searchable online through the county's deed search and in the public access room. Searches go fastest when you have three facts in hand:

  • The buyer's name (grantee) and the seller's name (grantor)
  • The year of the transaction
  • The tax parcel ID, which every conveyance filed here must now carry

Copies by mail need the book type and page number, and the office will not process a request without them. Pay by cashier's check, money order or attorney's check made out to the DeKalb County Clerk of Court. Certified copies can also be ordered through the eCertification portal, where an approved request must be paid within six days or it is rejected automatically.

  • Certified copy: $2.50 for the first page, 50 cents for each added page
  • Regular copy: $1.00 per page
  • Plat copy: $2.00 per page
  • Card payments on the fee chart page carry a surcharge of 2% plus $1.00

Can a seller still bring a deed to the DeKalb clerk's counter or mail it?

No. Since January 1, 2025, Georgia House Bill 1292 requires every real estate document in DeKalb County to be filed electronically, and mail-in recording is closed to new filings. The clerk accepts e-recordings from approved providers listed on its page, including Simplifile and CSC.

Anyone who is a party to the instrument and files on their own must also upload a government-issued ID at efile.gsccca.org, where it is verified before the filing can go through. The page cites O.C.G.A. 44-2-39(b)(1) for that step. Most sellers never touch this step, since the firm running the closing e-records the deed. If you are selling without an attorney, such as a family transfer, build the ID check into your timeline.

Plats follow the same electronic rule and have been e-file only since 2017, and UCC financing statements became e-file only in 2022.

What has to be in the package before the clerk will record a deed?

Every deed of conveyance needs a PT-61 transfer tax form and the tax parcel ID printed at the top of its first page. Georgia has required that parcel ID on DeKalb transfers and conveyances since July 1, 2019, under House Bill 694.

The PT-61 is completed online at the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority site, printed, and submitted with the deed. The clerk does not supply forms, the document must be complete before it arrives, and most documents need a signature, a witness and a notary. State identification is required for any filing.

One point sellers like: original documents are recorded immediately and handed back, per the clerk's citation of O.C.G.A. 15-6-72. The recording fee schedule is posted on the clerk's fee page as a Real Estate Fees chart. Georgia moved to flat filing fees in 2020 under House Bill 288, so get the current figure from the clerk or the closing firm instead of an older quote.

How much is the Georgia transfer tax and who pays it?

The seller owes it by law, though a sales contract often shifts it to the buyer. State revenue guidance gives the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 of the sale price, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fraction of $100.

Payment comes first; the clerk then attaches a certification that it has been paid. The governing statutes are O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10. For questions about exemptions, the Department of Revenue points people to the clerk of superior court in the county.

A separate intangible recording tax applies to a long-term note secured by real estate. The state's county facts page puts it at $1.50 per $500 of face value, and in DeKalb the clerk is the collector. A payoff and release on your existing loan is a cancellation of the security deed, and the clerk's page says more than 26,500 mortgages are cancelled in the county each year.

What recording deadlines and rules apply to DeKalb County documents?

Several documents carry a clock that starts when they are signed or when work ends. The clerk's real estate page lists the ones below.

DocumentRule on the clerk's pageAuthority cited
Deed of conveyancePT-61 and parcel ID required; transfer tax due at recordingO.C.G.A. 48-6-1, 48-6-2
Security deedDue 90 days after signing, or penalty and interest on intangible tax when the maturity is over three yearsO.C.G.A. 48-6-61
Foreclosure deedFile within 120 days of signing to avoid a $500 penaltyStated on the clerk's page
Materialmen's or laborer's lienFile within 90 days of the last work or materials; it expires 395 days after filing without a lawsuitO.C.G.A. 44-14-361, 44-14-367
Bond to discharge a lienClerk must approve the bond before it is recordedO.C.G.A. 44-14-364

Table source: DeKalb County Clerk of Superior Court, Real Estate page.

How can a DeKalb homeowner guard against a fraudulent filing?

The clerk participates in the Filing Activity Notification System, called FANS, run through the Georgia clerks' authority at fans.gsccca.org. Owners register their own parcels, or those of relatives, and receive an email when a deed, lien or similar paper is filed or indexed against it. Owners who signed up under the older DeKalb alert system had to register again for FANS.

Before a sale, a forged deed or a surprise lien turns up in the title search and can stall a closing. An alert is cheap protection for an inherited or vacant house. A veteran can also record a DD-214 discharge with the clerk at no charge, which keeps a certified copy on file locally.

What housing numbers frame a DeKalb County sale?

QuickFacts lists 337,059 housing units in DeKalb County in 2025 and 58.8% owner-occupancy for 2020 to 2024. Owned homes had a middle value of $357,800, tenants paid $1,692 in median gross rent, and builders took out 1,321 permits during 2025.

  • Median household income: $80,644 (2020 to 2024, in 2024 dollars)
  • Mean commute: 30.4 minutes
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and over: 47.4%
  • Foreign-born residents: 17.3%

DeKalb was formed in 1822 and lost its western half to Fulton County in 1853. Interstates 20, 85, 285 and 675 cross it, and MARTA rail serves the east and northeast lines. A house in unincorporated DeKalb, in Decatur, in Brookhaven or in Stonecrest all record at the same clerk's office, even though each sits under a different city government.

More questions about DeKalb County, GA Clerk of Superior Court

Must a seller travel to Decatur to file a deed?

No. Real estate documents in DeKalb County must be filed electronically, and self-filers upload a government ID at efile.gsccca.org first. The closing firm usually e-records for a sale.

Which side owes Georgia's transfer tax?

The seller is liable under Georgia law, though the contract can assign it to the buyer. The Department of Revenue rate is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents per added $100 or fraction of $100, paid before recording.

When must a security deed or foreclosure deed be recorded?

A security deed should be filed within 90 days of signing, and a foreclosure deed within 120 days, which the clerk's page ties to a $500 penalty if missed. Check dates with the closing attorney.

Where can I order a certified copy of a recorded deed?

Order through the eCertification portal, or mail a request listing the book type and page number. The clerk lists certified copies at $2.50 for page one and 50 cents for each added page, and an approved portal order must be paid within six days.

What is a PT-61 and why does the clerk require it?

It is Georgia's real estate transfer tax declaration, completed online and printed. Every deed of conveyance in DeKalb County must carry one, plus the tax parcel ID on page one, before the clerk can record it.

Douglas County by the numbers

What lands on the Douglas County clerk's desk?

Inside the Clerk of Superior Court's office, a Real Estate Division takes in deeds, liens, plats and UCC financing statements for Douglas County property, then indexes, scans and transmits them. The same division collects and passes along the associated charges, among them transfer tax and intangible tax. About 1,050 pages fit in one deed book.

Other filings in the same office can touch a sale. Federal, state and county tax liens and fi. fa. writs arrive through whichever agency issued them. Scanned real estate, UCC and civil protective order papers go on to the statewide cooperative authority, which also lists UCC filings on its website. A veteran's DD214 is recorded at no charge and is withheld from public view.

The county's records page sends land record and case file questions to the clerk at 770-920-7441, and sends wills and estate questions to Probate Court at 770-920-7249. Requests for other county documents run through an online JustFOIA portal that took over on March 30, 2026.

Who is allowed to file a Douglas County deed?

House Bill 1292 changed filing on January 1, 2025. Anyone outside a list of professions now has to e-file every deed and lien document, and the only channel is the state cooperative authority. An individual homeowner cannot hand a deed over the counter anymore.

The county defines a self-filer as a person who is not one of the following, and those groups keep their usual access:

  • Credit unions, mortgage lenders and mortgage servicers.
  • Georgia attorneys and Georgia surveyors.
  • Title insurers.
  • Georgia real estate brokers or salespersons.
  • Public officials.

Self-filers register at efile.gsccca.org, and that site is their only filing route. Questions go to 1-800-304-5174 or help@gsccca.org. For a home sale the simplest path is to let the closing attorney or title company record the deed.

How much transfer tax goes with a Douglas County deed?

A deed cannot be recorded until the real estate transfer tax is paid, and the clerk then certifies the payment on the document. The Georgia Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100, applied to the sale price.

Responsibility falls on whoever signs the deed or benefits from it. The department says the seller is liable, while adding that contracts frequently hand the cost to the buyer, so check that clause in yours. The PT-61 Real Estate Transfer Tax Declaration accompanies the filing and can be completed online through the cooperative authority.

Whether a given deed is taxable or exempt is a question for the clerk. The Revenue Department's 2026 legislative update describes HB 413 and transfer-on-death deeds: beneficiaries gain a right to the death certificate, those deeds rank ahead of unsecured debts, revoking one takes one witness rather than two, and no PT-61 is filed at recording, only later when the beneficiary records an acceptance affidavit.

How many documents does the Douglas County clerk record?

For 2024 the office counted 30,047 recorded instruments, which is 2,296 more than in 2023. Deeds and liens account for nearly all of it: the 11,692 lien filings sit not far behind the 16,563 real estate filings, while plats numbered only 203 and UCC financing statements 1,589. A title search on a Douglas County house therefore reads through a thick index, and checking early saves time at closing.

Behind those counts sit 154,293 estimated residents and 59,028 housing units at mid-2025. Owners occupy 66.9 percent of homes, and the Census Bureau puts a typical owned home at $296,900.

What are the clerk's recording fees?

A fee sheet on the county website, the version dated August 22, 2024, covers deeds, liens, UCC filings, plats, copies and civil filings. Its real estate section groups items by kind. Warranty, quitclaim, foreclosure, estate and security deeds sit with modifications, cancellations, affidavits and powers of attorney. Lis pendens, hospital liens, tax liens and lien assignments appear as their own group.

Schedules change, so confirm the current amount with the clerk before you budget. Transfer tax is calculated from the sale price and is billed apart from recording charges. Everything shows up on the settlement statement your closing agent prepares.

  • Recording charge: taken from the clerk's fee sheet.
  • Transfer tax: a state formula applied to the sale price.
  • E-filing for self-filers: arranged through the cooperative authority.

Which other Douglas County offices hold records on a property?

The clerk holds the recorded title documents, and several other county offices hold the rest of a parcel's paper trail. A seller who gathers them before listing answers most buyer questions in advance.

  • Appraisal Department: property record card, assessment notice and appeals, plus the deed specialist who updates ownership on the tax side.
  • Tax Commissioner: the tax bill, homestead exemption file, delinquent tax list and any tax sale notices.
  • Planning and Zoning: survey approvals for splitting or combining parcels and the Unified Development Code.
  • Geographic Information Systems Department: parcel maps and data requests.
  • Records Department: county government records that the clerk does not keep.
  • Probate Court: wills and estate files, relevant when a house passes to heirs.

The Records Department follows the Georgia Open Records Act. It charges no fee for the first quarter hour of staff time, bills later research at the hourly rate of the lowest paid qualified employee, and charges $0.10 per photocopy. Payment is by cash, check or money order made out to the Douglas County Board of Commissioners. Staff are not required to create a report or summary that does not already exist.

What if you want to divide a lot or sell the house?

Dividing a parcel begins in Planning and Zoning. The proposed survey goes to the Zoning Administrator, under Article 5, Section 502 of the Unified Development Code. Once the approved, stamped survey is recorded, the owners sign suitably titled deeds and record them through an attorney or the e-file system. The Appraisal Department's deed specialist, at 770-920-7430, handles the tax-record side.

A routine sale moves quickly. The seller signs a deed at closing, transfer tax is paid, and the clerk records the deed with its tax certification. The buyer's lender records a security deed after that. An old lien or lis pendens in the clerk's index would show up for the closing agent, who would ask for payoff first.

Heirs, owners with back taxes and landlords with tenants in place sometimes pick a no-repair sale. The recording steps are identical, and the buyer's closing attorney does the e-filing, so you never register as a self-filer.

More questions about Douglas County, GA Clerk of Superior Court

May I file a deed myself in Douglas County?

Only online. Since January 1, 2025, a person who is not an attorney, lender, servicer, title insurer, surveyor, broker or public official must e-file through the state cooperative authority, and the clerk does not take paper filings from them.

What rate does Georgia's transfer tax follow?

It is $1 for the first $1,000, plus 10 cents for each further $100 of the price, counting any fraction as a full unit. The seller is liable, although a contract often moves the cost to the buyer.

Which number covers Douglas County land records?

The Clerk of Superior Court, at 770-920-7441, covers land records and case files. Probate Court, at 770-920-7249, covers wills and estates.

Does a transfer-on-death deed need a PT-61 at recording?

No. The Revenue Department's summary of HB 413 says the form comes into play only when the beneficiary later records an acceptance affidavit.

Does the clerk charge veterans to record a DD214?

No. DD214 discharge records are recorded at no charge to the veteran and are no longer public record.

Fayette County by the numbers

How does the Fayette County clerk fit into a house sale?

At closing the clerk files the deed that carries title to the buyer, plus mortgages, releases, liens and plats. The office describes itself as the keeper of public records for the county, and Georgia has made the clerk a constitutional officer since the 1798 constitution.

The clerk also serves State and Magistrate Courts and, since July 1, 2010, runs the clerical side of the county Board of Equalization, which hears property tax valuation disputes. A seller therefore deals with this office twice over, once for the deed and any recorded lien, and again if a valuation appeal reaches the equalization board.

Fayette County was set up in 1821 as Georgia's 49th county, covers about 199 square miles south of Atlanta, and borders Fulton, Clayton, Spalding and Coweta counties. Deeds for property in Fayetteville, Peachtree City, Tyrone, Brooks, Woolsey and the unincorporated areas all record with this one clerk.

Where is the Fayette County clerk's office and when can I look at records?

The clerk is at One Center Drive, Fayetteville, GA 30214, and a postal box at P.O. Box 130. The main line is 770-716-4290, and the county's page lists 770-716-4291 for the Real Estate division.

Visitors can inspect records on weekdays between nine in the morning and five in the afternoon, holidays excluded. The clerk's search policy says deeds, liens and similar non-court papers are open to inspection under the Georgia Open Records Act, so no formal open records request is needed to look at them during those hours. Public computer terminals inside the office show images without staff supervision.

  • Property index search is on the clerk's Online Services page.
  • A property and mortgage fraud check alerts you when something is recorded against a registered parcel.
  • The court docket search covers Superior, State and Magistrate Courts.

Sign up a parcel for the alert if you hold an empty or estate-owned house in Fayette, since a forged deed or stray lien is easier to fix when caught early.

What does Fayette's clerk charge for real estate filings?

The clerk's court fee schedule, revised July 1, 2024, charges a flat fee for real estate filings. Amounts in the table come from that sheet; call the office to confirm them before paying.

Selected Fayette County clerk fees (court fee schedule revised July 1, 2024)
Filing or serviceFee
Recording a document pertaining to real estate$25.00
Cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment, each instrument listed$25.00
Plat, map or floor plan, each page$10.00
Lien, lis pendens, notice or bond$25.00
Tax lien by a state or local government agency$5.00
Certified copy of a document, per page$0.50
Each certification or exemplification with seal$2.50

The same schedule lists uncertified copies at $0.50 a page when you copy them yourself and $1.00 a page with staff help. For a certified copy of a deed, the clerk points people to the eCertification site at ecert.gsccca.org, and regular copies requested by email run $1.00 per page with payment in advance.

How can a Fayette County seller check the title record before listing?

Pull your own record first. The clerk's Online Services page offers a property index search, and the office keeps public terminals where recorded images can be viewed without staff supervision.

  • Look for an old security deed that was paid off but never cancelled of record.
  • Look for liens, lis pendens notices and tax liens filed against the owner's name, which carry $25.00 and $5.00 filing fees on the clerk's schedule.
  • Order a certified copy of the vesting deed through ecert.gsccca.org if a buyer's lender asks for one.
  • Check that every name on the deed matches the people signing the listing agreement.

When heirs are the sellers, call 770-716-4291 and ask what must be recorded ahead of the deed to the buyer. Sorting that out first costs less than a delay at the closing table.

Can I file a Fayette County deed electronically?

Yes, and for many documents electronic filing is now the expected route. The Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority writes in its real property guidelines that, with some exceptions, since January 1, 2025 deeds, liens, plats and other real property documents in electronic form are to be filed through the Authority's eFiling Portal. Paper documents go directly to the clerk.

The Fayette clerk's Online Services page links to eFiling for real estate and UCC documents through the Authority. Most sellers never touch it, since the attorney or title company running the closing e-records the deed. If you are handling a family transfer without a closing firm, ask the clerk's Real Estate division at 770-716-4291 whether a paper filing is accepted for your document before you drive over.

The Authority's filing page also says electronic filing is offered in participating counties, so a county's participation is a local decision. Confirm Fayette's current rules with the clerk before relying on either route.

What is the Georgia transfer tax and the PT-61 form in Fayette County?

A deed cannot be recorded until Georgia's transfer tax is paid, and the clerk then stamps a certification onto it. The rate in O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10 reads $1 on the first $1,000 or fraction of price, then 10 cents per further $100 or fraction.

The statute puts the liability on the seller, though contracts frequently hand it to the buyer. Exemption questions go to the clerk, so call 770-716-4290.

The PT-61 declaration is completed online with the Clerks' Authority. Print the finished form and hand it in with the deed; each applicable deed takes just one. Authority customer support, per the revenue department's page, answers at (800) 304-5174.

What recording rules apply to a mortgage payoff or intangible tax in Fayette County?

Paying off your lender leads to a release or cancellation of its security deed, recorded here at the $25.00 per instrument shown above. Ask the closing attorney to confirm yours was filed, since a loan still open of record can surface in a title search.

A new mortgage also triggers Georgia's intangible recording tax of $1.50 per $500 of face amount, with the security instrument recorded inside 90 days. The state says collection falls to the clerk in most counties and to the tax commissioner in others, so ask the Fayette clerk who handles it here.

The clerk's schedule lists a veteran's discharge record as no fee when valid identification is shown.

What housing numbers frame a Fayette County sale?

The Census Bureau puts Fayette County's population at 125,156 for July 1, 2025. Owners dominate the housing picture in the Bureau's 2020 through 2024 survey.

  • Owner-occupied rate: 80.1 percent.
  • Typical owned home: $436,400 in value.
  • Gross rent at the midpoint: $1,898 monthly.
  • Midpoint household income: $111,978.
  • Four-year college graduates among adults 25 and up: 49.9 percent.
  • Mean commute: 31.4 minutes.
  • Building permits in 2025: 435.

The recording fee is flat at $25.00, while the transfer tax rises with the sale price. The county says interstates 75, 85 and 285 are within reach and that MARTA service runs from nearby Fulton County, which matters to commuters who buy here.

More questions about Fayette County, GA Clerk of Superior Court

What will Fayette County charge to file my deed?

The clerk's fee schedule, revised July 1, 2024, lists $25.00 for recording a document pertaining to real estate. Releases and satisfactions are $25.00 per instrument listed, and plats are $10.00 a page.

Who pays the Georgia transfer tax on a Fayette County sale?

The seller owes it unless the contract says otherwise, and the clerk records the deed only after the tax is paid.

Where is the Fayette County Clerk of Superior Court?

The office is at One Center Drive in Fayetteville, and a postal box at P.O. Box 130, Fayetteville, GA 30214. Call 770-716-4290, or 770-716-4291 for the Real Estate division.

Can I look at a recorded Fayette County deed without a formal request?

Yes. The clerk's search policy treats deeds and similar papers as open under Georgia's Open Records Act, so a visit during public hours replaces a formal request.

Does the Fayette County clerk also handle property tax appeals?

Only partly. The clerk keeps the equalization board's files and sends its notices, but valuation appeals begin with the Board of Tax Assessors.

Forsyth County by the numbers

What does the Forsyth County Clerk of Superior Court record?

The clerk records and indexes real estate in Forsyth County: deeds, plats, condominium floor plans, UCC filings, General Execution Docket entries, lien filings and military discharges. A sale of any Forsyth County house, in Cumming or elsewhere, sends the buyer's deed to this office, along with the cancellation of your security deed once the loan is paid off.

The Real Estate division answers at 770-781-2120 (choose option 6) or at RealEstate@forsythco.com. The clerk's letterhead gives the courthouse address as 101 E. Courthouse Square, Cumming, GA 30040. The clerk's site also offers a property index search, a forms page, a link to a property and mortgage fraud check, and a map viewer for abstractors.

What are the Forsyth County clerk's recording fees?

A deed, quit claim deed or similar real estate document costs $25.00 to record, and extra pages are included. Security deed cancellations, releases and assignments are also $25.00 each. The table below repeats the lines most sellers meet at closing, taken from the clerk's posted schedule.

Selected Forsyth County clerk fees (Forsyth County Clerk of Superior Court, Court Costs and Recording Fees)
ItemFee
Deed, quit claim, modification, assignment of leases and rents (each)$25.00, added pages included
Security deed cancellation, release or assignment$25.00, added pages included

Certified copy$2.50 first page, $0.50 each added page

Call the Real Estate division for a total before mailing a check; this schedule shows the clerk's charge alone. Transfer tax and any intangible recording tax are billed separately.

Who pays transfer tax on a Forsyth County deed?

Payment comes first: the clerk stamps a paid certification onto the deed, then records it. The state rate works out to $1 on the opening $1,000 of price and ten cents per additional $100 or part.

Sellers owe it unless the contract says the buyer pays, and the settlement statement shows which happened. The PT-61 declaration is filed online through the state clerks' authority, and the Forsyth clerk's menu links to it. A question about exemptions goes to this clerk, as the Department of Revenue directs.

What is the intangible recording tax on a mortgage?

This is a separate state charge on lenders and borrowers, and a seller handing over a deed does not owe it. The security instrument behind a new loan has to be recorded within 90 days, and the rate the state prints is $1.50 per $500 of note, with a partial $500 counted in full.

Most counties route it through the clerk. Your settlement statement shows whether any of it applies to your closing.

How does e-filing a deed work in Forsyth County?

The clerk's site sends real estate e-filers to efile.gsccca.org. Since January 1, 2025, anyone who files real estate documents electronically there must upload government-issued photo identification, such as a driver's license or passport, and have it verified before the filing can go forward.

If you plan to bring a deed yourself, call the Real Estate division and ask which filing methods it accepts for your situation, plus how your payment should be made out. The clerk's FAQ page lists questions about checks, card payments, witnesses and notarizing, so check it before you drive to the courthouse.

How do liens, tax executions and unpaid property tax connect to the clerk?

When county tax goes unpaid the Tax Commissioner can issue a Fi.Fa., a lien that lands on the clerk's General Execution Docket. It lasts seven years unless paid off, and the payoff covers the tax plus fees, penalties and interest. A warning letter with a 30-day window comes first.

  • A lien on the docket is a public record, so expect it to be raised when the buyer's side searches title.
  • The cancellation is itself a filing at the clerk's counter, with the lien fee shown in the table above.
  • Any tax sale is an auction on the courthouse steps in Cumming, held on a first Tuesday.

The tax commissioner's property tax page also asks sellers to email the closing statement to the tax office so the next bill goes to the new owner's name, provided the purchase closed before November 15.

The PT-61 filed with the clerk does a second job for the buyer. When the property was not subdivided, changed or improved and the transfer tax was paid, the tax commissioner says that form can stand in as the new owner's property tax return, and the preceding year's final valuation is treated as the returned value unless a new return is filed with the Board of Assessors.

How do I get a copy of a recorded Forsyth County document?

The Copy Requests page quotes statutory prices under O.C.G.A. 15-6-77: half a dollar a page for a standard copy, a dollar a page for non-standard, and $2.50 for the first page of a certified copy with 50 cents per page after that. Non-standard means unscanned, odd-sized or atypical records that need hands-on help from staff.

You can also search the property index on the clerk's website to see whether a cancellation of your old security deed was filed. If it is missing, call your loan servicer first and then the Real Estate division.

What else does the Forsyth County clerk file that touches a home sale?

The same posted fee sheet that prices deeds lists a few other items owners run into. A veteran who needs a military discharge copy pays nothing but must show valid identification. Notary authentication costs $3.00, and a new or renewed notary commission is $55.00. Registering a trade name for a rental or flipping business costs $175.00 as a filing fee, which excludes newspaper publication.

Lawsuits are a separate track. The clerk's civil division in Superior and State Court takes e-filings through two vendors, PeachCourt and a Tyler Technologies portal, and the E-File page links to both. A lawsuit over a sale contract would start there instead of at the Real Estate counter.

What do the Census numbers show for Forsyth County sellers?

Census Bureau QuickFacts counts 282,805 residents in Forsyth County as of July 2025, a 12.5 percent gain since April 2020, on roughly 224.62 square miles of land. The housing stock totals 98,879 units, and owners live in 84.4 percent of occupied homes. Homes that owners occupy have a median value of $550,400 (2020 to 2024 survey), while the typical household earns $143,784.

With values that high, a clean deed and a paid-up tax account matter a great deal to a buyer's lender. The clerk's office is in the courthouse at the county seat, Cumming.

  • Median gross rent in the same survey was $2,090.
  • The county issued 1,743 building permits in 2025.
  • Foreign-born residents make up 22.9 percent of the population, and 27.7 percent speak another language at home.

More questions about Forsyth County, GA Clerk of Superior Court

Where does a Forsyth County deed get recorded?

The clerk's Real Estate division, in Cumming. Phone 770-781-2120 and choose option 6, or write to RealEstate@forsythco.com.

What is the Forsyth County recording charge for a deed?

$25.00 for a deed, quit claim or similar document, and added pages cost nothing extra. Transfer tax is a separate charge.

Who owes the Georgia transfer tax on a sale?

The seller, unless the sales contract moves it to the buyer. The state requires payment before the deed is recorded.

Do I need ID to e-file a real estate document in Georgia?

Yes. Since January 1, 2025, anyone e-filing real estate documents through the Georgia clerks' portal must upload government-issued ID and pass verification first.

Can an unpaid tax bill stop my Forsyth County sale?

It can slow one down. A recorded Fi.Fa. on the clerk's docket is public and stays until the tax, fees, penalties and interest are paid, so get a payoff figure from the Forsyth County Tax Commissioner before closing.

Fulton County by the numbers

Which Fulton County office records my deed?

Deeds for Fulton County property are recorded and indexed by the clerk's Real Estate Division, part of the office of the Clerk of Superior and Magistrate Courts. It also handles lien filings, plats, condominium floor plans, military discharges, partnerships, trade names and Uniform Commercial Code filings.

The Deeds and Records Room sits on the ground floor of the Lewis Slaton Courthouse in Atlanta and holds instruments that reach back to the early 1800s. The Real Estate Recording customer service line is (404) 613-5313. Mail for the Record Room goes to 136 Pryor St., CG13, Atlanta, GA 30303.

How fast does the Fulton County clerk process a recorded deed?

Documents delivered on paper are processed within four weeks of receipt, and documents sent through an eRecording vendor or the state clerks' authority are processed in two to three business days. The clerk's site also carries a land records update page that reports progress on processing, so check it when timing matters for a closing.

After recording and processing, the original documents come back to you by mail. That gap is wide enough that you should ask whoever runs your closing how they plan to submit the deed. The clerk names three vendors: SimpliFile, eRecording Partners Network and Corporation Service Company (Ingeo).

What does the Fulton County clerk charge to record real estate documents?

A deed or any other instrument pertaining to real estate costs $25.00. Each cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment is also $25.00 per instrument listed on the filing. The Real Estate Division does not accept credit cards for real estate transactions; it takes cash, business checks and money orders.

Fulton County clerk real estate fees (Fulton County Clerk of Superior and Magistrate Courts, fee schedule dated July 1, 2024)
ItemFee

The same schedule lists other recording lines, such as $5.00 for the first page of an instrument not otherwise specified, so ask the division which line fits your document before you send payment.

The same clerk's office issues notary commissions: $55.00 in person for a new or renewed commission, or $60.00 for a renewal by mail. A certificate of authority is $2.00. The office also runs a Georgia records search for real estate and notary records, listed on its site next to the court record searches.

How is Georgia transfer tax collected on a Fulton County sale?

No deed gets recorded here until transfer tax is settled. The state charges a flat $1 on the first $1,000 of price, then a dime for each further $100 or fraction thereof.

Responsibility falls on the seller by default, and a clause in the sales contract can hand it to the buyer. The PT-61 declaration is filed online through the clerks' authority, whose support line for filers is (800) 304-5174. Whether a given transfer is exempt is a question for this clerk, according to the state.

How do I search or copy Fulton County land records?

Visit the Deeds and Records Room and use its computer lab, or search from home on the state authority's website, which the clerk says costs $5 for four hours of access. Staff cannot do legal research by phone. For questions about a deed or lien index, you either search it yourself or hire a title search company.

  • Certified copies must be ordered through eCertification at ecert.gsccca.org, which delivers a secure PDF by email after you approve payment.
  • Plain copies can be ordered the same way, around the clock.
  • By mail, send a letter naming the document type and its book and page number. The clerk's FAQ lists $1.00 a page for plain copies and $2.50 for the first certified page plus $0.50 for each added page.

If you cannot find a recorded cancellation of your old loan, ask your servicer for a copy and then check the index.

What do tax liens and tax appeals cost at the Fulton County clerk?

Tax liens filed by a state or local agency have their own pricing: $5.00 for page one, $2.00 for every page after, and $2.00 more for each cancellation, release, notice or withdrawal that references the original. Federal tax liens, materialman's liens, lis pendens and writs of fieri facias fall under the $25.00 lien and General Execution Docket line instead.

Property owners who take a county tax appeal to superior court will find a $25.00 County Tax Appeal line in the clerk's court-cost table. The assessor's notice and the board that hears the first appeal come before that step, so start with the county's assessment office and the notice it mailed you.

Transfer tax is billed on top of every figure above. If the deed is the only thing you are recording, the $25.00 fee and that tax are the two numbers to plan around.

What about intangible recording tax and foreclosure sales in Fulton County?

A lender financing the buyer's purchase pays a separate intangible recording tax, which the state prices at $1.50 for every $500 of the note, with part of $500 counted as a whole.

Foreclosure sales are a separate public process. The clerk's FAQ says properties sold in Fulton County are advertised once a week for four weeks in the legal notices of Fulton Neighbor Newspapers. Auctions run monthly on the first Tuesday, with bidding hours from 10:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. at the courthouse steps.

  • Anyone behind on a mortgage should get the scheduled sale date from the servicer in writing.
  • A sale that has already been advertised still leaves time to sell the property or work out a plan, but that window is short.

What does the Fulton County housing picture look like for sellers?

Fulton County is a large urban county with over a million people. Census Bureau QuickFacts shows 1,098,791 residents in July 2025 across 526.70 square miles of land, with 534,663 housing units. Owners occupy just 54.3 percent of the homes, which leaves rentals as a big slice of the market.

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $458,800 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, set against median gross rent of $1,732 a month. Median household income was $95,292. Builders pulled 9,660 permits in 2025. The county counts 462,481 households averaging 2.26 people each.

Sellers of a rental or inherited house should line up the recorded deed history before listing, because a missing cancellation or an old lien is easier to clear before a buyer's title search finds it.

More questions about Fulton County, GA Clerk of Superior Court

Which Fulton County office takes a deed for recording?

With the Real Estate Division of the Fulton County Clerk of Superior and Magistrate Courts in Atlanta, or through an approved eRecording vendor. The customer service number is (404) 613-5313.

How much is the Fulton County deed recording fee?

The fee schedule dated July 1, 2024 lists $25.00 for a deed or any instrument pertaining to real estate, plus $25.00 for each cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment.

Does the Fulton County clerk take credit cards for real estate recording?

No. No. Pay with cash, a business check or a money order.

How quickly does Fulton County record a deed?

Paper documents are processed within four weeks of receipt. Documents sent through an eRecording vendor or the state authority are processed in two to three business days.

When are foreclosure sales held in Fulton County?

Monthly, on the first Tuesday, with sales running 10:00 a.m. through 4:00 p.m. at the courthouse steps. Notice appears weekly for four weeks beforehand, per the clerk's FAQ.

  • E-filing: an eFile Real Estate Records page on the court site routes filers to the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.
  • Costs: the Fees page under the Real Estate Division is where to confirm recording charges before a deed goes in.

What transfer tax applies to a Henry County deed?

Think of the transfer tax as a one-time toll on the sale itself, apart from the yearly property bill. The clerks' authority says it comes due before recording, after which the clerk attaches proof of payment. Sellers carry it unless the contract assigns it elsewhere.

The authority's help page prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 (or a fraction of $100 to $1,000), then 10 cents for every further $100 or fraction. The PT-61 form words it as tax due at .10 per $100, minimum $1.00. Because the state sets the rate, Henry charges the same as every other county.

How do I prepare the PT-61 for a Henry County closing?

Fill it out on the clerks' authority website. The e-filing is free and takes no account. Print the one-page confirmation, carry it to the closing, and if the closing succeeds, hand it in with the deed package. One PT-61 accompanies each deed. Nobody signs it, but the filer ticks a box attesting that the data is true and correct to the best of their knowledge.

  • County is always required, and city matters when the lot lies inside municipal limits.
  • The map and parcel field is mandatory, though N/A is accepted when no number exists.
  • The seller line should name the prior owner rather than a listing agent or auctioneer.
  • A mistake caught after filing goes to the clerk's office. One caught beforehand means a new form and a discarded old one.

The authority's help desk answers at 800-304-5174. Land that straddles a county line needs its own deed and PT-61 in each county, with consideration divided between them and an affidavit describing the split. Exemptions from paying the tax are programmed into the form, which displays the legal basis for any you pick.

How do Henry County property taxes connect to recording?

The annual property bill is a separate matter, yet a sale touches it. Henry's Tax Commissioner bills the owner of record on January 1 and files a lien against that person unless a settlement statement turns up within 90 days of the due date, per Georgia Code 48-3-3. Statements are emailed to propertytax@henrycountyga.gov. The bill page prints November 16 as the due date, with mailing by mid-September.

A third charge attaches to loans. State revenue officials say a long-term note secured by real estate must have its security instrument recorded where the land lies, within 90 days, and the intangible recording tax runs $1.50 per $500 or fractional part of the note's face amount. Most counties let the clerk collect it and others use the tax commissioner, so ask Henry's office which one applies before a refinance or a buyer's mortgage closes.

  • Transfer tax: normally the seller's, paid when the deed is recorded.
  • Intangible recording tax: follows the lender's security instrument and does not arise in an all-cash purchase.
  • Property tax: billed to the January 1 owner, backed by a county lien.

QuickFacts lists 264,922 Henry County residents for July 2025 and 97,759 housing units on 318.71 square miles of land. With 1,666 building permits issued in 2025, new-build deeds and plats pile up next to resales, which keeps the real estate desk occupied.

  • Owners live in 74.9% of occupied homes.
  • The county counts 86,704 households.

The county's financial report puts it about 25 miles southeast of Atlanta, with McDonough, Stockbridge, Hampton and Locust Grove inside its borders. A deed for a house in any of those cities goes to the same county clerk.

Which other Henry County clerk services come up around a sale?

Liens are the usual surprise. The state revenue department explains that county tax liens and state tax executions are filed in the clerk's office on the general execution docket, and the Henry clerk's court services menu lists Writs of Fieri Facias (FiFa). If a title search turns up a lien, get a payoff figure before closing.

  • FANS: the Filing Activity Notification System has its own page under the Real Estate Division.
  • Notary Public: the Real Estate Division menu includes notary information.
  • Uniform Commercial Code: a separate filing category in the same menu.
  • Trade Names: the menu lists trade name filings for sellers who operate a business under a registered name.

Ask the closing agent whether any judgment, tax execution or recorded lien names the seller. If one does, clear it before the deed is signed and have the release recorded with the clerk afterward.

What should I verify before the deed is submitted?

Collect the legal description, map and parcel number, and the names exactly as they read on the previous deed. The state form insists on the parcel data. Confirm the transfer tax figure and who is paying it with the closing agent, because the contract can move that cost off the seller.

  • Find out whether the closing agent will e-file or deliver paper.
  • Make sure a payoff and release are lined up for any security deed.
  • Pull the plat if the lot was split recently. The clerk's Plats page covers copies.
  • Ask the Tax Commissioner whether a lien or unpaid current bill exists.

After recording, the deed book and page are cross-referenced to the PT-61 reference number. The authority passes PT-61 data to the state revenue and audit departments weekly, and the form is the trigger for the ownership change on the county tax rolls.

More questions about Henry County, GA Clerk of Superior Court

Where do I file a deed in Henry County?

File with the Clerk of Superior Court's Real Estate Division. The clerk's court pages show Deeds and Liens, Fees, Locating Records and an eFile option for real estate records through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.

Who pays transfer tax on a Henry County sale?

The seller, unless the contract says someone else will. The clerks' authority states $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents per further $100 or fraction, due before the clerk records the deed.

Is a PT-61 required to take a name off a deed?

Yes. The clerks' authority says any change in ownership calls for one, even when no money moves, unless the paper is a security deed, a release, a qualifying lease or an affidavit. Some changes also escape the tax itself.

Does a transfer on death deed need a PT-61?

Not when it is recorded, because nothing has been conveyed yet. Once the owner dies and the beneficiary files an affidavit accepting the real estate, the form is needed.

How can I look up a recorded Henry County deed?

Start with Locating Records under the Real Estate Division, which describes searching deeds, liens and property records online. Contact the clerk's office when an older instrument does not turn up.
